rounds.text: Pasupati Acrylon carries substantial execution and financial risks, highlighted by significant cost overruns in its recently commissioned 150 KL per day grain-based ethanol project, where total capital outlays escalated from an initial estimate of Rs. 167 Crore to approximately Rs. 188 Crore due to civil work difficulties [E32, E33]. This heavy capital expenditure, funded via Rs. 104 Crore in term loans and internal accruals [E33], translates into heightened financial leverage just as the company enters a business segment where ethanol prices are entirely determined by Oil Marketing Companies with no pricing control given to the company [E44]. Furthermore, the lack of Minimum Selling Price adjustments poses direct threats to forward planning, capacity utilisation, and return on invested capital [E45]. Compounding these operational hurdles, institutional money flow registers a negative signal (-0.05 percentage point holding change) [E4], the board opted against recommending any dividend for FY 2024-25 [E40], and the historical record features a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -58.9% [E10]. Conceded: the company records a high relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E8] alongside sector tailwinds in chemicals [E21].
